confirmedSourceFindings.finding: Global service flags and policy digests exist but no exact-tenant/cohort/effect admission ledger in inspected published paths.
Calendar token/data fetches omit redirect:error; an exact physical attempt budget must address automatic redirects.
Actual primary Calendar ID is read after token exchange and retained as targetId/targetHash; proposed policy must bind to it.
Main access/number/voice/texting engines/providers differ from published source. Older cleanup/authentication repairs cannot be assumed deployed or wholesale copied.
Prior live StageA closed before owner signup; exact challenge already consumed before rejected exchange. Earlier consumer/session and live root cause remain unknown.

calendarFirstCandidateAcceptance.requiredOutcome: No policy, malformed policy, expired policy or global flag only permits zero token/data/provider fetches.
Named tenant admitted; another tenant, same-slug replacement, changed owner email/key or lifecycle cannot consume quota or dispatch.
Changed Google client identity or actual primary Calendar target denies new work. Literal primary is not account identity.
Status/start/complete, direct standalone API, refresh, foreground worker, scheduled wave, recovery and dispatch all apply the same fence.
Existing one-use state/PKCE, original verified session, epoch, expiry and tenant/lifecycle checks remain mandatory; wrong session/state makes no token request.
Two concurrent admissions for last request slot cause at most one physical request; independent category and total limits cannot overflow.
Durable CAS reservation precedes fetch. Storage unavailable or ambiguous CAS acknowledgment cannot produce an unmetered attempt.
Timeout/HTTP failure/crash after admission consumes quota. Retry/reconciliation consumes another permitted attempt; no reset/refund/replacement create.
Policy revoke, expiry, brake, disconnect, pause or lifecycle change between reservation and effect prevents the physical request without restoring quota.
Token/data requests reject redirects or meter and validate each hop; no default-follow hidden requests or credential/code forwarding.
Retained intents, bookings, outbox and jobs are bounded/inventoried; changed or partial census prevents rollout and unrelated retained work cannot resume.
Exactly one deterministic test event ID is used; lost-create reply, 409 and later reload reconcile it without another event.
Remote metadata, exact target and ETag prevent changing unrelated or manually conflicting events.
Failed/deferred Calendar operation retains authoritative local visit and exposes waiting/retry/needs-attention without declaring sync.
Canceled/removed visit cannot create a late event; pause/disconnect stop new writes while keeping exact outstanding IDs and receipts.

Explicit cleanup scope and budget permits only known test-owned event/resource reconciliation/deletion; does not admit create, send, token to other target or new contacts. Expired ordinary policy must not strand unclear recurring resources.
No OAuth code, token, verifier, credential, account identifier or unrestricted policy document leaks into DTO/URL/log/receipt; store hashed bindings only where adequate.
Owner/admin distinguish unavailable, customer action needed, waiting approval, limit reached and actual receipt-confirmed active; one named pilot never makes other tenants appear available.
Calendar-only fence cannot authorize Twilio/Vapi/managed SMS/model/email. These require their complete transport fences and separately accepted budgets before gates change.
Exact candidate includes only intended changes based on05e; focused local proof is separate from one approved publication and named actual Calendar/signup/provider acceptance.
